slides.title: Starter Activity: 6-Cell Knowledge Retrieval

starterQuestions.q: What does it mean when error bars representing 95% Confidence Intervals overlap between two trial arms?
starterQuestions.a: There is generally no statistically significant difference between the two treatments at the p < 0.05 threshold.

starterQuestions.q: What is the formula for Absolute Risk Reduction (ARR)?
starterQuestions.a: ARR = Control Event Rate (CER) - Experimental Event Rate (EER).

starterQuestions.q: How is Relative Risk Reduction (RRR) calculated from ARR and CER?
What is the difference between Standard Deviation (SD) and Standard Error of the Mean (SEM)?
starterQuestions.a: SD quantifies biological dispersion/spread among individuals; SEM estimates the precision of the sample mean relative to the population mean.

starterQuestions.q: Why is a double-blind protocol essential in phase III drug trials?
starterQuestions.a: To eliminate both participant placebo effect and investigator observation/allocation bias during outcome assessment.

starterQuestions.q: Describe a biological relationship demonstrating 'saturation kinetics'.
starterQuestions.a: Enzyme-catalyzed reaction rates plateauing at V_max as all active sites become occupied by substrate (Michaelis-Menten kinetics).

courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology

objectives.knowledge: Differentiate statistical significance metrics: SD vs SEM vs 95% CI, p-values, and statistical power.
objectives.application: Calculate Absolute Risk Reduction (ARR), Relative Risk Reduction (RRR), and Number Needed to Treat (NNT) from RCT clinical datasets.
objectives.evaluation: Critique graphical trends for saturation plateaus, linear proportionality, and distinguish random biological variation from clinical effect.

terminology.def: Gold-standard experimental trial where participants are randomly assigned to experimental or control cohorts.
A range of values around a sample statistic that has a 95% probability of containing the true population parameter.
The simple arithmetic difference in event rates between control and experimental treatment groups (ARR = CER - EER).
The proportional reduction in adverse event rates in treated vs untreated patients [RRR = (ARR / CER) × 100%].
